l4_steps.name: Ingest daily BSP/ARC ticket sales data feed
l4_steps.input: IATA BSP Interactive Sales Report (ISR) file; ARC TicketExpress settlement file
l4_steps.output: Raw ticket coupon dataset loaded to revenue accounting staging area
l4_steps.kpi: File ingestion success rate ≥99.5%; processing time <2 hours after BSP file drop
l4_steps.pain_point: BSP file format differences across IATA billing regions (e.g. BSP-Americas vs BSP-Europe) cause parsing errors for non-standard fare constructions; legacy ASCII flat-file format has no structured error reporting

l4_steps.name: Match ticket coupons against PSS booking records
l4_steps.input: Raw coupon dataset from step 1.1; Altéa booking and coupon status records
l4_steps.kpi: Automated coupon match rate ≥97%; unmatched coupons backlog <3% of daily volume
l4_steps.pain_point: PNR purge cycle (typically 90 days post-departure) removes booking records before interline billing arrives, causing match failures for delayed interline invoices; no automated re-match queue

l4_steps.name: Apply ATPCO fare basis code validation
l4_steps.input: Matched coupons with fare basis codes from step 1.2
l4_steps.output: Validated fare constructions; flagged error report for non-compliant coupons
l4_steps.kpi: Fare validation error rate <1% of total coupons processed; validation completed within 4 hours of ingestion
l4_steps.pain_point: ATPCO fare filing publication lag (up to 48 hours after filing) means recently-sold fares may not yet appear in validation tables, generating false-positive errors on new fare products launched during peak sale windows

l4_steps.name: Resolve coupon validation exceptions
l4_steps.input: Flagged exceptions from steps 1.2 and 1.3; fare construction rules; Altéa reissue records
l4_steps.output: Resolved exception log; adjusted coupon records cleared for proration
l4_steps.kpi: Exception resolution within 5 business days; exception backlog <500 coupons at any time
l4_steps.pain_point: Manual exception handling volume spikes after IROP events when re-issued tickets carry non-standard fare constructions and waiver codes not recognised by the revenue accounting system; resolution requires coordination with airport and contact centre teams

l4_steps.name: Calculate interline revenue proration
l4_steps.input: Validated interline coupons; IATA Resolution 850e proration rules; bilateral proration agreements
l4_steps.output: Prorated revenue splits per operating carrier segment; interline billing receivables
l4_steps.kpi: Proration processing completed within T+3 calendar days; interline dispute rate <2% of prorated billings
l4_steps.pain_point: IATA Resolution 850e proration formula conflicts with bilaterally-negotiated prorate agreements for specific carrier pairs; manual overrides are required and not fully auditable within REVERA, creating reconciliation risk

l4_steps.name: Apply ASC 606 revenue recognition rules
l4_steps.input: Prorated revenue data from step 2.1; flight departure confirmation records from Amadeus Altéa PSS
l4_steps.output: Revenue recognition schedule; deferred revenue journal entries for untravelled portions
l4_steps.kpi: Deferred revenue posting accuracy ≥99.9% of ticket value; period-end deferred revenue balance reconciled within T+5 business days
l4_steps.pain_point: Ancillary revenue bundling (e.g. seat upgrade + checked bag + base fare sold as one fare family) requires performance obligation disaggregation under ASC 606 Topic 606; the revenue accounting subledger does not support multi-element arrangement splitting natively, requiring manual journal overrides

l4_steps.name: Process EMD ancillary and ancillary revenue
l4_steps.input: Electronic Miscellaneous Document (EMD-A and EMD-S) records; ancillary sales data from direct channel
l4_steps.output: Ancillary revenue postings by product category; EMD redemption log
l4_steps.kpi: EMD-to-revenue match rate ≥98%; ancillary revenue posted within T+2 days of service delivery date
l4_steps.pain_point: EMD-A (associated, tied to flight coupon) vs EMD-S (standalone, sold independently) misclassification causes ancillary revenue to be booked to incorrect income lines; the distinction is not enforced at point of sale by all booking channels

l4_steps.name: Reconcile BSP billing memo vs internal records
l4_steps.input: IATA BSP billing memo for the settlement period; internal validated coupon dataset from Phase 1
l4_steps.output: Reconciliation variance report; list of net billing differences by agency and fare code
l4_steps.kpi: Net billing variance <0.1% of total settlement amount; reconciliation completed within T+1 business day of BSP memo receipt
l4_steps.pain_point: Currency conversion timing differences between the BSP billing date and the internal booking date create systematic variances in markets with volatile FX rates (e.g. ARS, TRY, EGP); IATA BSP Link applies the exchange rate at billing date, not booking date

l4_steps.name: Raise Agency Debit Memos for billing discrepancies
l4_steps.input: Reconciliation variances from step 3.1 exceeding tolerance; agency IATA codes and billing references
l4_steps.output: Agency Debit Memo (ADM) or Agency Credit Memo (ACM) records filed in IATA BSP Link
l4_steps.kpi: ADM filed within IATA 15-day filing deadline; ADM acceptance rate by agencies ≥85% within 30 days
l4_steps.pain_point: IATA BSP Link ADM filing requires exact citation of the IATA resolution code authorising the ADM; incorrect or missing resolution citations cause automatic rejection, restarting the 15-day clock and risking write-off if the deadline cannot be met on re-submission

l4_steps.name: Approve and submit BSP settlement payment
l4_steps.input: Reconciled net BSP settlement amount; IATA bank account details; dual-approval workflow
l4_steps.output: Approved payment batch instruction; bank transfer confirmation to IATA clearing account
l4_steps.kpi: Payment submitted on BSP settlement value date with zero late-payment penalties; settlement accuracy 100% of approved net amount
l4_steps.pain_point: Dual-approval workflow between Revenue Accounting and Treasury creates a bottleneck when approvers are unavailable on the BSP settlement date; SAP S/4HANA workflow does not support time-sensitive escalation routing to backup approvers

l4_steps.name: Confirm BSP settlement receipt and archive
l4_steps.input: Bank MT940 payment confirmation; IATA settlement acknowledgement
l4_steps.output: Closed billing period record; settlement archive with audit trail
l4_steps.kpi: Settlement confirmation archived within 24 hours of IATA acknowledgement; audit trail completeness 100%
l4_steps.pain_point: IATA BSP Link does not provide real-time payment confirmation; reconciliation relies on bank MT940 SWIFT message feeds which may lag by 1 business day, leaving the settlement status in IATA BSP Link as 'pending' and triggering false escalation alerts

l4_steps.name: Post revenue journal entries to SAP General Ledger
l4_steps.input: Recognised revenue data; proration outputs; ancillary postings; deferred revenue adjustments
l4_steps.output: Posted journal entries; GL revenue accounts updated with passenger and ancillary revenue
l4_steps.kpi: Automated posting rate ≥95% of journal lines; manual journals <5%; posting completed within T+2 business days of period end
l4_steps.pain_point: Revenue accounting system to SAP interface uses scheduled batch file transfer; if a batch fails mid-run, partial postings create out-of-balance GL entries requiring manual reversal journals and repost, delaying period close

l4_steps.name: Perform revenue GL account reconciliation
l4_steps.input: Posted SAP GL balances; subledger data from Mercator REVERA Revenue Accounting
l4_steps.output: Signed-off account reconciliation with variance commentary; open items list
l4_steps.kpi: All revenue GL accounts reconciled within T+5 business days of month end; unexplained open items <$50,000 aggregate
l4_steps.pain_point: High volume of open items from ongoing interline billing disputes strains the reconciliation process; open item ageing is not automatically surfaced in BlackLine, requiring manual export and pivot analysis, often pushing sign-off past the T+5 target

l4_steps.name: Generate revenue reports and close accounting period
l4_steps.input: Reconciled SAP GL balances; management reporting templates; prior-period comparatives
l4_steps.output: Revenue flash report delivered to CFO; accounting period locked in SAP S/4HANA
l4_steps.kpi: Revenue flash report delivered to CFO within T+3 business days of period end; period close completed by T+7 business days
l4_steps.pain_point: Parallel month-end close activities (cost accounting, payroll, procurement AP) contend for SAP period-close resources; lock conflicts on shared profit centre and cost centre objects delay period close when multiple finance teams post simultaneously
